outputs: adversarial prompts to trigger unsafe content generation
The paper focuses on generating adversarial prompts to trigger unsafe content in text-to-image and text-to-text models, which is a form of natural language generation aimed at red teaming.

changes_made.explanation: Removed redundant 'Prompt Generation' task, normalized model names, added Stable Diffusion as a key target model, and simplified output descriptions
Normalized ROUGE-L to ROUGE base form as per guidelines, kept other metrics as they are specific classifiers used in the paper
No LLM-as-judge evaluation used; the paper uses classifiers (Q16, NudeNet, TOXIGEN) for safety evaluation, not LLMs for quality assessment
No human evaluation conducted; the paper explicitly states they use automatic classifiers to fully automate the red teaming process

overall_notes: The paper focuses on automated red teaming using FLIRT framework. Key NLG aspects include adversarial prompt generation for text-to-image and text-to-text models. Evaluation uses safety classifiers (Q16, NudeNet for images; TOXIGEN for text) and toxicity detection (Perspective API). The extraction was generally accurate with minor normalization needed.
